title: Two ways out: home fire planning
h1: Two ways out: home fire planning and rehearsal
dek: You may have less than two minutes. How to map your home, find two exits from every room, plan for children, older adults and people with disabilities, and rehearse until it is habit, from USFA, NFPA and FEMA.
description: A home fire escape plan from USFA, NFPA and Ready.gov: smoke alarms, two ways out of every room, a meeting place, rehearsal, and plans for each person in your home.
recheck: Immediately if USFA, NFPA or Ready.gov revise their escape-planning guidance; otherwise at the next quarterly source sweep.

source_use.usfa-fire-escape: Less than 2 minutes to escape; map with all doors and windows; two ways out of every room; keep exits unblocked; outside meeting place in front; practice with everyone; test button starts the drill; high-rise sequence.
source_use.shelter-nfpa-smoke-alarms: Alarm placement, monthly testing, 10-year replacement, interconnection, meaning of alarm sounds, devices for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, the 60 percent / in half inconsistency.
source_use.shelter-ready-home-fires: Fire speed; smoke and toxic gases; battery and unit replacement; windows, screens and security bars; practice in the dark; wheelchair doorways; feel doors; crawl low; cannot get out; stop, drop and roll; burn first steps; after a fire; heater, stove, candle and extinguisher prevention tips.
source_use.shelter-nfpa-escape: One or two minutes; floor plan and alarms marked; meeting place; street number; memorize fire department number; assign helpers and backups; security-bar releases; guests and sleepovers; practice twice a year; children's drills; wake-up check; ladders; low under smoke; closing doors; sealing yourself in; stay out; high-rise 'defending in place'.
source_use.shelter-cpsc-co: If a CO alarm sounds, get outside to fresh air and call 911.
source_use.shelter-ready-disabilities: Neighbors who can assist with building evacuation; backup mobility devices.
source_use.shelter-ready-plan-locations: Ask for building alarm, evacuation and shelter-in-place plans; high-rise exits, elevators, stairwells.
source_use.shelter-cdc-power-outage: Flashlights over candles; candles away from flammables and never unattended.
source_use.shelter-ready-plan: Household plan questions including shelter, evacuation and communication; practice with the household.
